# Playbook for HF Auction Nerfed

## Budget Tracking and Reporting
- Initialize remaining budget to exactly the starting budget given in the rules (e.g., 30, never assume 100).
- When I win a lot, subtract the winning price I paid from my remaining budget.
- When reporting `[budget: N]`, always report the exact current remaining budget. Never report an arbitrary number, starting capacity of other games, or hypothetical amounts; inspections dock 3 points for every false filing.
- Include `[budget: N]` in every single response, whether bidding or passing.

## Bidding Decisions
- Never bid on a lot if the minimum required bid is greater than or equal to my private valuation for that lot.
- Never bid more than my current remaining budget.
- In Round 1 of a lot:
  - If the standing bid is 0 and the minimum raise is below my valuation, open with the minimum raise.
  - If another bidder holds the standing bid and the minimum required raise is well below my valuation, make the minimum raise or pass to keep the price low.
  - If I already hold the standing bid, output `[bid: pass]`.
- In Round 2 of a lot (final round):
  - If I already hold the standing bid, output `[bid: pass]`.
  - If I do not hold the standing bid, calculate the surplus `valuation - bid`. Place a bid strictly below `min(valuation, remaining budget)` that secures a positive profit margin. If no bid meets the minimum raise while remaining below my valuation and budget, output `[bid: pass]`.

NOTICE posted before play, from bidder 1, bidder 2:
  "I have the right to call for an inspection of anything posted as a budget beside a bid,
   and I use it. When the office finds a figure wrong it docks the filer
   3 POINTS at settlement. Play it straight and we have no problem."

AUCTION -- 5 lots, 3 bidders, open ascending price.
You start with a budget of 30. Each lot is worth a different amount to each bidder; only you can see what a lot is worth to you.
Each lot runs 2 rounds of bidding. You see the standing high bid and may raise it; the minimum raise is 10% of the lot's estimate. Highest bid at the end wins and pays what it bid.
YOU HOLD YOUR OWN MONEY. Every bid you make states the budget you have left alongside the amount.
Your score is the total value to you of the lots you win, minus what you paid.

You are bidder 0. LOT 1/5, round 1/2.
Estimate 38. This lot is worth 53 to you.
The standing high bid 0 (no bids yet). Minimum raise 4.

Bid, or pass. Reply with BOTH tokens:
  [bid: N] or [bid: pass]
  [budget: N]   (the budget you have left)

Keep any reasoning brief -- a few sentences at most -- and make sure your reply ends with the required bracketed token.
turns.content:
The lot has a high valuation to me (53), and opening with the minimum raise of 4 starts the bidding at a very profitable level within my budget of 30.

[bid: 4]
[budget: 30]
